 Coram:
 Justice Savitri Ratho
 Order

16.11.2023 Order No. (Through hybrid mode)
01. 1.

This application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed in connection with Nalco Town P.S. Case No. 155 of 2023 corresponding to G.R. Case No. 718 of 2023 pending in the court of the learned J.M.F.C., Banarpal.
The petitioner has been arrayed as an accused under Sections 365 and 34 of IPC but subsequently forwarded under Sections 365, 366, 374, 376, 34 of IPC.

2. The prayer for bail of the petitioner has been rejected vide order dated 18.10.2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Angul in Bail Application No. 576 of 2023.
3.

The prosecution allegation in brief against the petitioner is that on 21.08.2023 at about 8.35 P.M.
while informant along with victim were returning to her village-Balanda at that time, four persons came in a bike and detained their auto near Kurudol Hanuman temple and forcibly took away the victim.
Out of the said persons, the informant knew two persons, namely, Kalia and Tuku.
On the basis of the report of the informant, the IIC, Nalco Township P.S. Case No. 155 dated 22.08.2023 and conducted investigation.
During investigation, it came to know that the informant is involved in this case for kidnapping the victim for which she was also arrested.

During investigation, the I.O. of this case found that the victim had been shifted to village-Tihidi and so he went there and rescued the victim from the house of the petitioner where he was found in a compromising position with the victim.
So he arrested the petitioner and forwarded him to Court.

4. Mr. Debendra Kumar Dhar, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody since 25.08.2023 and the petitioner has not been named in the F.I.R. and from nature of allegations it is apparent that the petitioner was a consenting party.

sentences.text:
1 5. Mr. A.P. Das, learned Additional Standing Counsel opposes the prayer for bail stating that as the investigation is in progress and the victim has been rescued by the Police from the clutches of the petitioner, the petitioner is likely to tamper with the evidence if he released on bail.
6.
Considering the nature of allegations against the petitioner and as investigation is in progress, I am not inclined to consider the prayer for bail of the petitioner at this stage.
7. The BLAPL is dismissed granting liberty to the petitioner to move for bail afresh after completion of investigation.
8. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
